On Tue, Jul 22, 2025 at 09:12 AM Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@payforge.com> wrote:
> We started seeing a spike in tail latency and intermittent 503s against our reserved capacity around 08:55 PDT.

Triage update (quick):
- I pulled the scheduler logs and queue metrics for the reserved slice. Around 08:50 we saw a sustained rise in per-request GPU time on 4 hosts serving PayForge—avg token processing increased ~3x compared to baseline.
- No explicit OOMs, but KV cache miss rate increased sharply (possible model context jump from customer traffic).
- Neighboring tenants didn't show a correlated spike; however, kernel selection changed (fallback to a slower kernel on one Canary node) during a rolling config push 08:35–08:48. That change looks like the likely trigger.

Interim mitigations I can do now:
1) Pin PayForge requests to non-Canary hosts (hotfix routing) — ~10–12m to push. Expected to reduce 95p latency significantly.
2) Enable automatic fallback to a quantized model variant for the hot path (adds some quality risk, reduces GPU time ~40%) — ~8–10m.
3) If PayForge approves immediate burst, we can allocate extra reserved slots from our burst pool (billing approval required) for up to 2 hours.

Recommendation: Do 1 immediately and 2 as a second stage. If business-critical throughput still degraded, authorize a short burst while we roll back the Canary kernel change. I will prepare an ops summary for Naomi to use in the exec note.

Jonas Weber
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
